stories.body: The United States resumed strikes inside Iran after a five-night pause, saying it hit dozens of Revolutionary Guard command centres and missile, drone, coastal-defence and maritime sites in response to an Iranian attack on US forces in Jordan. Iranian media reported civilian deaths on Qeshm island and the Revolutionary Guard said three of its members were killed. Iran then launched missiles toward Jordan and Kuwait, where one worker was killed, while drone attacks set fire to two gas vessels at Egypt's Damietta port. Mediators say they are still trying to revive talks, but the renewed fighting has intensified fears that the conflict could spread across the region. Analysts say Tehran may see a contained conflict as a way to retain leverage over shipping routes and sanctions rather than accept a ceasefire that leaves it economically isolated.
stories.headline: US and Iran exchange major strikes as regional war threatens to widen

stories.body: Poland is investigating debris and a 10-metre crater near Tarnawa Kolonia, about 92 kilometres from Ukraine, after an object entered its airspace during a large Russian assault on Ukraine. Prime Minister Donald Tusk said recovered fragments most likely came from a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile and that it was armed, though he said Poland was probably not the intended target. Poland scrambled an F-16 after detecting the object, and NATO said it remained in close contact with Polish authorities and would take necessary steps to defend alliance territory. The incident came as Russian strikes killed at least eight people in Ukraine, with some reports placing the toll higher.
stories.headline: Poland investigates suspected Russian missile strike as NATO jets scramble

stories.body: Hot, dry and windy conditions across the EU have been 43% more severe this year than the average for the same period over the past two decades, according to European fire-monitoring data. About 435,000 hectares have burned in roughly 1,400 fires, around triple and more than double the respective historical averages. France and Spain have begun to see some relief as major blazes near Bordeaux and west of Madrid stabilise, allowing many evacuees to return, but fires remain active in Greece, Portugal, Turkey and the UK. Researchers say climate change has more than doubled the number of fire-prone summer days in southern Europe since 1981, with France and Spain especially affected.
stories.headline: Wildfires spread across Europe as extreme fire weather breaks records

stories.body: The death toll from Tuesday's magnitude-6.8 earthquake in Kumamoto prefecture on Japan's southern island of Kyushu has risen to 30, with at least 62 people injured. Nearly 5,000 Self-Defence Forces personnel are assisting searches at a damaged shopping centre, a paper mill and collapsed homes while temperatures reach 35C and continuing aftershocks complicate rescue work. Six of the 12 people pulled from rubble at an Aeon shopping centre have died after a gas explosion, while eight workers died after a chimney collapsed at a paper mill. Tens of thousands of homes remain without power or water, and about 15,000 people are in shelters.
stories.headline: Japan earthquake death toll rises as aftershocks and heat hamper rescue efforts

stories.body: Colin Gray, the father of Apalachee High School shooter Colt Gray, has been sentenced to 15 years in prison after giving his son the gun used in the Georgia school shooting. The case concludes the latest in a series of prosecutions seeking to hold parents criminally accountable when they fail to prevent their children from carrying out mass shootings.
stories.headline: Father of Georgia school shooter sentenced to 15 years for providing gun

stories.body: The Ninth US Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that the Trump administration cannot deny immigrants arrested inside the United States an opportunity to seek release on bond while their immigration cases are pending. The 2-1 ruling rejected the administration's broad interpretation of a 1996 immigration-law provision, with a Trump-appointed judge joining the majority. The decision deepens a circuit split: four other appeals courts have rejected the policy, while the Fifth and Eighth Circuits have backed it, increasing the chance that the Supreme Court will decide the issue.
stories.headline: Appeals court rejects expansion of mandatory immigrant detention

stories.body: Former Wisconsin Lieutenant Governor Mandela Barnes has withdrawn from the Democratic primary for governor, saying it had become clear who the party's nominee would be, without naming a rival. His exit follows polling that showed progressive state lawmaker Francesca Hong leading with 38% support, ahead of Barnes on 16%, and came as party officials prepared for reports concerning unverified allegations about Barnes's conduct. Barnes's campaign said there were no allegations of misconduct or wrongdoing against him. Moderate Democrats hope his departure can help consolidate support behind Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley, though Hong remains the clear front-runner.
stories.headline: Mandela Barnes drops out of Wisconsin Democratic governor primary

stories.body: Spain will deploy military personnel to support the Civil Guard after thousands of migrants crossed from Morocco into the North African enclave of Ceuta, largely by swimming around the Tarajal border breakwater. At least nine or 10 people were reported dead, while authorities said the influx had mounted over recent days and included young men, women with babies and minors. Madrid has reinforced police and maritime resources, while Morocco's ambassador said both governments were in contact and that Morocco wanted those who crossed to return. Spain's Interior Ministry says trafficking networks amplified a Supreme Court ruling that prevents immediate border returns for migrants intercepted at sea.
stories.headline: Spain deploys military after thousands of migrants cross from Morocco into Ceuta

stories.body: Spain has ended the national level-3 wildfire emergency for Madrid and Ávila, returning operational control to regional authorities after conditions improved; Toledo had already been downgraded. The government said the emergency response, the first national declaration of its kind for wildfires, had been effective, although military and firefighting resources will remain available. Major fires continue elsewhere, including near Fermoselle in Zamora, where two of the most dangerous fronts have stabilised but active sectors, hot spots, evacuations and worsening heat-and-wind forecasts remain a concern. The EU is coordinating firefighting aid as high fire risk spreads across much of Europe.
stories.headline: Spain’s wildfire emergency eases in Madrid and Ávila, but major fires continue elsewhere

stories.body: The Madrid regional government has put up for sale a 485-square-metre luxury penthouse in Chamberí that it bought in April for temporary institutional meetings during planned renovations to its Puerta del Sol headquarters. The reversal came less than a day after the purchase became public and drew criticism over its undisclosed price, intended use and location near regional president Isabel Díaz Ayuso's home. The government says it will sell the penthouse along with four Gran Vía properties, aiming to raise €20 million for reconstruction after fires in the Sierra Oeste. Opposition parties say the sale followed public exposure of the purchase and are demanding the full file and cost.
stories.headline: Madrid reverses course and will sell Ayuso’s luxury penthouse office

stories.body: Spain has led a multinational operation to identify and remove extremely violent illegal online material linked to The Com, a decentralised transnational network associated with groups that promote violence and social collapse. Police found 4,340 links, with Spain's counterterrorism and organised-crime intelligence centre detecting more than 2,800 of them, mainly on TikTok and Telegram. The content included self-harm, suicides, violent assaults, child sexual abuse and animal cruelty. Europol has warned that the network and related groups use social media, gaming platforms and messaging services to recruit, radicalise and exploit children and young people.
stories.headline: Spain leads police operation against violent online network ‘The Com’

stories.body: Barcelona prosecutors had asked a court to issue protection measures for the two children of a woman allegedly killed by her husband in Sant Martí, but the judge rejected the request. The earlier case arose from the husband's complaint that the woman had abused him and their children, and prosecutors said they sought a protective order and alternative housing for the mother because the family situation appeared objectively concerning. Prosecutors appealed after the decision, but the appeal had not been resolved before the killing. Friends said the 34-year-old victim, Camila, feared her husband and had been due to begin divorce proceedings the following day; investigators believe the children may have witnessed the killing.
stories.headline: Prosecutors had sought protection for children before fatal gender-based killing in Barcelona

stories.body: Catalonia's traffic authority is testing an AI-equipped mobile camera system to detect drivers using phones and vehicle occupants not wearing seat belts correctly. The pilot, conducted in June and July on the A-2 near Cornellà de Llobregat and the AP-7 near La Roca, detected more than 8,500 suspected cases of phone use and more than 4,500 seat-belt violations. The authority estimates that 3.6% to 6.6% of observed drivers used a phone and 1.3% to 1.8% of occupants used seat belts incorrectly. Officials say the technology still needs further training and reliability improvements, but they hope to include it in the 2027-2030 road-safety plan.
stories.headline: Catalonia tests AI system to detect mobile-phone use and missing seat belts in vehicles

stories.body: Two century-old modernist buildings on Consell de Cent Street, the Casa Sebastián Bosch Elías and Casa Frederic Sanés, are being demolished to make way for the northern expansion of Barcelona's Glòries Park. One building has already been razed and the other is nearly gone. Neighbourhood groups had sought heritage protection but did not succeed, although they acknowledge that the demolition is tied to the wider park project. The expansion will affect about 80 properties, add 26,400 square metres of green space and create an urban terrace with play areas, pétanque courts and a multipurpose space; roughly 50 families have been rehoused or compensated.
stories.headline: Two modernist buildings demolished for expansion of Barcelona’s Glòries Park

stories.body: Catalonia's territorial commission has given final approval to Mollet del Vallès's new urban plan, which will guide development through 2040 and calls for 2,950 new homes, including 1,552 protected homes. Combined with existing and planned projects, the municipality expects to reserve 4,132 homes for social-housing policies as its population approaches an estimated 58,500. The plan prioritises contained growth and regeneration, with El Calderí set to receive about 1,406 homes, and also reserves land for industrial and logistics activity. It includes green corridors connecting Gallecs to the Besòs River and transport measures intended to reduce the barrier effect of the AP-7, C-17 and railway lines.
stories.headline: Mollet del Vallès approves plan for 3,000 new homes, half of them protected housing
